findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. On this point the page works.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: A link to the next step appears in the header, so a newcomer doesn't have to scroll through the whole study to find out what to do.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The install path is concrete: clone, prerequisites (git 2.40+, a C linker, curl, Claude Code or npm), `./setup.sh`, then `athena ask "add a changelog"`. It does not say whether a Claude account or API key is needed, or which repository Enter runs against (presumably the current directory).

At Athena's own URL, almost all of the page describes a different project, firstmate. Athena's main promise, a commit traced to the request, models, cost and verdict, is described but never shown. A newcomer sees the study feature, not the core product.
findings.source: Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: This link sits in the header with no explanation of who the "owner" is. A first-time visitor is not the owner and may be confused by it.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: Each state is listed as a bare name with a tag and citations, such as "close-pending waiting". What it means is only in the Glossary further down, so the list says little on its own.
findings.source: States of a piece of work

findings.text: The Counters entry names transitions by id before the reader reaches the Transitions section, and the ids are not links. This makes the dense middle of the page harder to follow.
findings.source: places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11

findings.text: Some transition cards pack several conditions into one long sentence. A newcomer who wants a rough idea of firstmate will likely skip the Transitions section.
findings.source: t4 ready → done — Guard: worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; ...

findings.text: The "Start here" section is a good on-ramp. It defines terms before using them, gives a one-sentence summary of firstmate, walks through one task in numbered steps and lists what has no limit. A newcomer can understand firstmate from this section alone.
The page says plainly where its sources are silent (in scope, retry limits, the captain's deadline). This supports Athena's claim to be traceable and builds trust.
findings.source: in scope: The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it.

findings.text: This limit describes Athena's own revision history (what a first reading missed) rather than a limit of the study. A newcomer has no context for it, and the "not run" tag only partly fits.
findings.source: f3 — A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths: ...

findings.text: The page mentions a `studies/` folder but gives no link or repository path. A newcomer can't find the source data from here.
findings.source: About this page: ... the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from.
